cases.question: Two convergent lenses of focal lengths 20 cm and 10 cm, separated by 30 cm; point object 30 cm before the first. Find image distance from the second.
derived: Fix lens L1 at x=0 and L2 at x=+30 cm; object at x=-30 cm
First image at x=+60 cm (30 cm right of L2, virtual object for L2)
Final ideal image at x=37.5 cm, which is +7.5 cm right of L2
illustrativeChoices: Choose a single point emitter on the optical axis (y=0); the question does not state an object's transverse extent
Choose 20 cm aperture for each ideal lens, finite full-circle ray sampling, relative source brightness 0.08; none is supplied by the question
cases.analysisPolicy: Run general native tracing; additionally apply existing ideal-thin-lens-geometric analytical model only because the accepted components satisfy its one-source ordered coaxial lens scope. Do not call the native trace an image-position detector.

cases.question: Two point sources 24 cm apart; find lens position for a converging lens of focal length 9 cm so their images coincide.
derived: Choose sources at x=0 and x=+24 cm (translation-invariant coordinates)
Lens can be at x=6 cm or x=18 cm, between sources
The common ideal image is respectively at x=-12 cm or x=+36 cm
illustrativeChoices: Point-source y=0 for both, illustrative 20 cm lens aperture, full-circle emission and relative brightness 0.08 for each
Current native two-source detector data have no per-source image provenance; both candidate scenes are examples to visualize after the inverse derivation
cases.analysisPolicy: Independent thin-lens algebra derives the two positions. Validate and execute both native candidate scenes, but do not claim general tracing analytically proves identical image locations.

cases.question: Converging lens f=+5 cm in contact with diverging lens f=-10 cm. Find combined focal length.
stated: Two zero-separation thin lenses with f1=+5 cm and f2=-10 cm
cases.nonExecutionReason: The validator rejects coincident ideal-lens planes. One equivalent lens f=+10 cm is a disclosed analytical reduction, not a native two-lens contact simulation; the question supplies no point source.

cases.question: Three lenses f=+10 cm, -20 cm, +9 cm; gaps 15 cm and 5 cm. Find the point where a parallel incoming beam converges after the third lens.
derived: Paraxial ABCD matrix from just before L1 to just after L3 has C=0
An exactly collimated input leaves exactly collimated: there is no finite convergence point (at infinity) in the ideal paraxial model
cases.nonExecutionReason: Current authorable point sources have finite positions and angular cones; a true parallel beam at infinity is not available. A distant point emitter would be only an approximation.

cases.question: Plano-concave lens with intensity-dependent material index mu=mu0+aI; determine intensity when f=2r.
stated: Refractive index depends on incident light intensity
cases.nonExecutionReason: The current ideal lens takes a prescribed focal length and has no intensity-dependent refractive index or nonlinear material interaction. Do not invent a lens or calculated intensity to make native execution succeed.

cases.question: Two equal-focal-length convergent lenses separated along x by 3f, but the second lens optical axis is displaced vertically by d (d much less than f); incoming beam is parallel. Find focus coordinates relative to first lens centre.
stated: Both lenses have focal length f
Second lens at x=3f with axis centre y=d
Parallel incoming light; d much smaller than f
derived: Paraxial focal location after lens 2: x=5f, y=2d relative to the first lens centre
For an initial ray height h: after L1 slope -h/f, at L2 y=-2h, after L2 slope (h+d)/f; at x=5f the ray height becomes 2d
cases.nonExecutionReason: Current ideal-lens authoring requires each lens vertically centred at y=0; the current source contract also lacks an exact collimated beam. No approximate/fake aligned scene is offered.
